historical_reviews.deepseek: It preserves the source's HTTP header check but does not verify that UBB is the selected platform's real Chassis instance or that a non-listed error status is unacceptable.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Its classification and OEM mapping gate are accepted, with success tightened to one supported 2xx Redfish collection response rather than merely excluding three codes.

historical_reviews.v3_1: The literal UBB identifier is project/firmware-specific and must be proven from the target's Chassis collection or approved mapping before testing its Sensors child.

original_test_intent: Verify that the intended platform exposes the approved UBB Chassis Sensors collection, returns a successful Redfish response rather than HTTP 400/404/405, and provides schema-consistent sensor members/readings without changing thresholds or chassis state.
original_method: Resolve the UBB member mapping from the target collection/firmware profile, perform one trusted GET to its Sensors child, validate a supported 2xx JSON collection and inspect approved sensor metadata under redaction.
manual_activity: The platform/BMC owner confirms that the selected target and firmware map the intended UBB hardware to `/Chassis/UBB`, supplies the expected sensor inventory/units/threshold policy, and approves sensor evidence retention.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Validated UBB member link or approved firmware mapping
Expected UBB sensor inventory, units and health/threshold baseline
Sensor-data redaction and secure evidence policy
safety_requirements: Do not assume literal UBB is valid on every firmware
Require supported 2xx instead of excluding only 400/404/405
Do not alter thresholds or settings
No chassis action or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Resolve and verify the UBB chassis mapping
Issue one bounded Sensors collection GET with headers/status
Validate approved member readings, units, status and thresholds against profile
Export redacted evidence and no-mutation audit
engineer_actions: Approve UBB mapping and sensor access
Provide expected inventory/units/threshold baseline and redaction

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The URI and header capture fit the source, but ipmitool is unrelated, `-k`/basic-auth are unsafe, and checking only 400/404/405 would accept other errors or malformed non-Redfish bodies.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With the approved UBB mapping, trusted TLS and secret-safe read credential, GET /redfish/v1/Chassis/UBB/Sensors once, require the documented 2xx/content type, validate collection/count/member links and approved sensor schema/units/status, then export redacted evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source URI, HTTP 400/404/405 rejection and 15/10 timing remain; UBB identity and expected sensors are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Prove the firmware-specific UBB member first, then validate its Sensors collection as both an HTTP contract and a telemetry inventory with exact schema, units, status and threshold semantics.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects package/TLS handling and strengthens a three-code exclusion into positive Redfish response and sensor-profile validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Generic Chassis checks prove neither the UBB mapping nor sensor inventory/reading semantics; this case does not exercise threshold writes or reset actions.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sensor readings are time-varying and vendor fields may use OEM units; acceptance needs capture timestamps and an approved profile rather than invented numeric limits.

project_override_considerations: A vendor Redfish client is equivalent only if it preserves the exact UBB URI, certificate verification, HTTP header/status evidence, raw collection topology and sensor unit/status semantics; ipmitool SDR output is not equivalent to this endpoint contract.
expected_evidence: Immutable BMC endpoint, firmware and approved UBB mapping
Certificate/trust and secret-provider result without secrets
Timestamped HTTP status/headers/content type and raw response hash
Proof of no HTTP 400/404/405 and supported 2xx Redfish body
SensorCollection count and unique in-scope links

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The authoritative item, URI, GET method and criteria consistently target the UBB Sensors collection and explicitly reject 400/404/405. DeepSeek's ipmitool label is a reference-review error, not a Master contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The endpoint and read behavior are identifiable. The UBB mapping, firmware profile, trust, credential, schema and expected sensor policy are concrete prerequisites; absence on the confirmed target is a test result.

review_improvement: Binds the OEM UBB path to the actual firmware and turns a narrow error-code exclusion into positive HTTP/Redfish collection and sensor-semantic evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Avoiding 400, 404 and 405 alone could still accept 401, 403, 500, a redirect or an HTML error page. The response must positively satisfy the firmware's supported 2xx and Redfish JSON contract. Before that, UBB must be resolved as the intended Chassis member because instance names are implementation-specific. Sensor validity then depends on collection link integrity and profile-defined reading units/status/threshold fields at a recorded time, not on readability alone.
